title: Group Safari Cost, Worked Out Per Person for Groups of 2, 4, 6 and 12
meta_title: Group Safari Cost Per Person: What Groups Really Save
meta_description: What a group safari cost really is per person: what shared vehicles save, what fees never drop, and worked Kenya examples for groups of 2 to 12.
excerpt: A group safari cost per person falls as vehicles, guides and transfers are shared, then levels off at about six per vehicle. Here is the maths, with worked Kenya examples.
content:
A group safari cost per person is often 15 to 20% lower than for a couple, because the vehicle, guide and fuel are shared. For a week in Kenya at mid-range camps, expect roughly US$2,550 to US$3,900 each for six people in one 4x4, against US$3,150 to US$4,700 for two (estimates).

If you are the one collecting names for a club, family or office trip, everyone will ask you the same question: what will I actually pay? This guide breaks a group safari cost into the parts that fall as your numbers grow and the parts that never move, with worked examples, country-by-country fees and the group policies we use. For the wider planning steps, start with how we organise a group safari from first headcount to final payment.

Quick Facts

  • Typical saving: The vehicle, guide and fuel bill splits between everyone, so per-person cost falls until each vehicle is full
  • Best value point: About six travellers per 4x4, which still gives everyone a window seat
  • Fixed per head: Park fees, gorilla permits, lodge beds and light-aircraft seats
  • Free place: The seventh place is free for every six paying travellers
  • Masai Mara fee: US$200 per adult per day July to December, US$100 January to June (checked November 2026)
  • Payments: 30 to 40% deposit, balance two to four weeks before travel; each traveller can pay separately

What Does a Group Safari Cost Per Person in Kenya?

A group safari cost in Kenya for seven days, with two nights in Amboseli, one at Lake Naivasha and three in the Masai Mara, comes to roughly US$2,550 to US$3,900 per person for six travellers at mid-range camps from July to December. A couple pays about US$600 to US$800 more each.

The table below shows how we build that figure. Park fees are the official non-resident rates; the vehicle and lodge bands are typical ranges, not a Divulge price list, and they move with dates, camps and group size. Treat this group safari cost table as a planning guide and ask for a real quote before you collect money from anyone.

Group sizeVehiclesVehicle share eachEstimated total per person
2 travellers1US$875-1,225US$3,150-4,700
4 travellers1US$440-615US$2,700-4,100
6 travellers1US$290-410US$2,550-3,900
12 travellers2US$290-410US$2,550-3,900, before free places

Each row adds the same US$780 in park fees (Amboseli at US$90 a day for two days, the Masai Mara at US$200 a day for three) and US$1,500 to US$2,700 for six nights in mid-range camps sharing a room, to an estimated US$250 to US$350 a day for a private Land Cruiser with driver-guide and fuel over seven days. Notice that the per-person price stops falling at six: a second vehicle for twelve costs as much as the first.

Which Costs Fall as Your Group Grows?

The costs that fall as a group grows are the ones charged per vehicle or per trip, not per person: the 4x4 and driver-guide, fuel, airport transfers, private guides for walks or city tours, and the crater fee in Tanzania. Fill every seat and this part of the group safari cost gets cheaper for each member.

Vehicles, guides and fuel

The vehicle is the line that changes most. One Land Cruiser costs much the same whether two people or six ride in it, so on a road safari it is usually the biggest saving in a group safari cost. We plan about six travellers per vehicle for groups, which keeps a window seat for everyone and room on the floor for camera bags.

Transfers and private extras

Airport pick-ups, a private guide in Nairobi, a bush dinner set-up or a boat on Lake Naivasha are priced per trip or per boat, so a full group pays less each. This is why club safaris and family group safaris often add private extras that a couple would find too expensive.

The free seventh place

On our group bookings, the seventh place is free for every six paying travellers. A group of seven pays for six, and a group of fourteen pays for twelve. Organisers either use the place themselves or spread its value across the group, which takes another chunk off the average group safari cost per head.

Which Costs Stay the Same Per Head?

Park and conservancy fees, gorilla and chimpanzee permits, lodge beds and meals, light-aircraft seats and visas are charged per person, so they never get cheaper as the group grows. On most trips they make up well over half the bill, which is why the group safari cost falls less than people expect.

In Kenya, the Masai Mara National Reserve charges non-resident adults US$200 a day from July to December and US$100 from January to June, with children aged 9 to 17 at US$50 (checked November 2026). Amboseli and Lake Nakuru cost US$90 a day and Nairobi and both Tsavo parks US$80 (checked October 2026). Our guide to Kenya park fees lists the rest, and Kenya Wildlife Service publishes the official tariff, so check it before you book.

Group safari cost in high and low season

Season moves the group safari cost more than group size does. Moving a Kenya trip from August to February halves the Mara fee, saving US$300 per person on a three-day stay, and many camps drop their rates too. Twelve travellers making that one change save about US$3,600 on Mara fees alone.

Rooms and single supplements

Lodge rates are quoted per person sharing a room, so the rooming list matters. Two friends sharing a twin pay the base rate; someone who wants a room alone pays a single supplement, which some camps waive outside peak months. For a week in camps it can add more to one person's bill than the vehicle saving gives back, so settle rooming before you share prices. Our Masai Mara safari cost guide shows typical camp bands by budget.

How Much Does Each Country Add to the Bill?

Each country adds a different fixed cost per person, and it decides the floor of any group safari cost. Kenya and Tanzania are driven by daily park fees, Uganda and Rwanda by gorilla permits, and Botswana and Namibia by lodge rates and flights more than by entry fees.

CountryMain fixed cost per personGroup angle
KenyaMasai Mara US$100-200 a day; Amboseli US$90Road safaris let six share one vehicle
TanzaniaSerengeti US$82.60 per 24 hours; Ngorongoro US$70.80US$295 crater fee is per vehicle, so it splits
UgandaGorilla permit US$800Permits sell out; book the whole group at once
RwandaGorilla permit US$1,500No group discount; under-15s cannot trek
BotswanaMoremi and Chobe P270 a dayLight-aircraft seats are per person
NamibiaEtosha N$280 a day plus N$60 per carLong drives make one shared vehicle good value

Tanzania fees are TANAPA and Ngorongoro rates checked October and November 2026; see our Tanzania park fees breakdown and the Tanzania National Parks site. Uganda and Rwanda permit prices were checked November 2026, and Botswana and Namibia fees the same month. Fees change, so confirm them before booking.

On a gorilla trip, the permit can be close to half of each person's group safari cost, so the saving from sharing shrinks. Our post on group gorilla trekking in Uganda explains how we split a large group across gorilla families and days.

How Many People Per Vehicle Gives the Best Price?

Six people per vehicle gives the best price on most group safaris, because a standard safari Land Cruiser seats six or seven and six keeps every traveller at a window. Seven fills the vehicle but squeezes someone into a middle seat, and eight means a second vehicle.

The awkward sizes are seven, eight and thirteen. Seven can fit in one vehicle if everyone accepts a tight squeeze; eight needs two vehicles at four each, which costs each person more than six in one. When your number lands just above a full vehicle, the group safari cost per head jumps, so we look at a larger vehicle, an extra night to spread the cost, or a free place that softens the jump.

Photography and birding groups often want fewer people per vehicle, three or four, so everyone has space to shoot or use a scope. That raises the group safari cost per head, but it is the single biggest factor in what each member actually sees and photographs.

Road safari or fly-in?

A fly-in safari saves days on the road but trims less off the group safari cost, because every light-aircraft seat is per person and the camp provides the game-drive vehicle. A road trip is where groups gain most. Our 7 day Kenya incentive safari flies, while the 6 day Kenya family safari drives with the same driver-guide throughout, and both can be priced for your numbers.

Insider Tips

  • Fix the headcount early: Lodges hold group rooms for a set time, so a firm number gets you a firm price
  • Ask for prices at two sizes: A quote at your target size and at the minimum shows what happens if two people drop out
  • Count vehicles, not just people: Seven travellers may need two vehicles, which can cost more per head than six
  • Travel January to June in Kenya: The Masai Mara fee halves, saving US$300 per person on a three-day stay
  • Agree rooming before quoting: Twin shares keep the group safari cost down; single rooms add a supplement
  • Keep extras optional: Balloon flights and spa time paid only by those who want them stop the base price creeping up

How Do You Get an Accurate Group Quote?

You get an accurate group safari cost by giving the operator four things: your travel month, a realistic headcount range, the rooming split and the budget tier. With those, a quote can show the price per person at each size, so nobody is surprised if two people drop out.

Ask for a group safari cost breakdown that lists park fees, permits, vehicles and lodges as separate lines, plus what is excluded: international flights, visas, insurance, tips and drinks. If your group has a corporate side, our corporate incentive safari team can also add venues, branding and awards dinners.

For payments, a deposit of 30 to 40% holds the booking and the balance is due two to four weeks before travel. Each traveller can pay their own share and arrive on different flights, which takes a lot of pressure off the organiser. You can compare all our options on the group safaris page.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a group safari cost per person?

A group safari cost per person for a week in Kenya at mid-range camps is roughly US$2,550 to US$3,900 for six in one vehicle, against US$3,150 to US$4,700 each for a couple (estimates, July to December). Park fees, beds and permits stay per head; the saving comes from shared vehicles.

Are group safaris cheaper than private safaris for two?

Yes. A private group safari is usually cheaper per person than a private safari for two, because one vehicle, driver-guide and fuel bill are split between more people. The saving levels off once each vehicle is full, at about six travellers, and our free seventh place for every six paying travellers lowers the average further.

Do gorilla permits get cheaper for groups?

No. Gorilla permits are fixed per person and have no group discount. Uganda charges US$800 and Rwanda US$1,500 per foreign non-resident (checked November 2026), so on a gorilla trip the permit is the biggest single line in the group safari cost. Big groups also need to book early, because each gorilla family takes only eight trekkers a day.

Does the group leader travel free on a safari?

The group leader can travel free if the group reaches the size for a free place. On our group bookings the seventh place is free for every six paying travellers, so an organiser who gathers six paying friends, colleagues or club members can use that place or share its value across the whole group.

How far ahead should a group pay for a safari?

A group safari is usually held with a deposit of 30 to 40% once the itinerary is agreed, and the balance is due two to four weeks before travel. Each traveller can pay their own share separately. Book six to twelve months ahead for July to October or for gorilla permits, since rooms and permits run out first in those months.

Final Thoughts

A group safari cost comes down through shared vehicles, guides and transfers, and the saving peaks at about six per vehicle. Fees, permits and beds stay per head, so season and rooming matter as much as numbers. Settle those, then ask us for a per-person quote at two group sizes.
